pr_title: roachprod: implement spot vm preemption detection for AWS.
pr_body:
Spot vm preemption detection is not implemented for AWS. Implemented spot vm detection for AWS using ec2 describe-instances and CloudTrail events. Whenver a spot vm is evicted by AWS instance description will have information related to isntance-state, instance-lifecycle and state-reason-code. If describe instance is called after 1 hour of instance termination then there is a fallback on cloud trail events.

Fixes: #126917
Epic: CRDB-10428

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/126925)

>fallback on cloudTrail as the instance is not available after 1 hour of termination

Does this mean that it can take up to an hour for `describeInstances` to show a terminated instance or that it takes at least one hour for it to show up?

If it's the former, then do you know ball park how often it fails?

If it's the latter, that seems quite unfortunate. I imagine many (most?) test would fail fast if a vm gets preempted, well within the one hour mark. Is there a reason to not just use cloud trail in all cases? Looks like it costs money, presumably that's why?

> > fallback on cloudTrail as the instance is not available after 1 hour of termination
> 
> Does this mean that it can take up to an hour for `describeInstances` to show a terminated instance or that it takes at least one hour for it to show up?

It is none of the case. What i meant is if we do `describeInstances`  after 1 hour of instance termination then it will throw error `InvalidInstanceID.NotFound` in that case there is a fallback on cloudtrail events. DescribeInstances show a terminated instance in real time as soon as the instance is terminated.
> 
> If it's the former, then do you know ball park how often it fails?
> 
> If it's the latter, that seems quite unfortunate. I imagine many (most?) test would fail fast if a vm gets preempted, well within the one hour mark. Is there a reason to not just use cloud trail in all cases? Looks like it costs money, presumably that's why?

There is a delay of around 1 minute to 15 minutes in propagation of events to cloudtrail. As most of the test will fail as soon as vm is preempted and a call to `GetPreemptedSpotVMs` will be made therefore `describeInstances` would give the information about the instance termination. But just in case if call to `GetPreemptedSpotVMs` is made after 1 hour of instance termination then we get information from cloudtrail.
I see thanks for clarifying, in that case it seems unfortunate to need it but a fallback makes sense.

2c:

To reduce complexity, I think we'd be pretty well covered with just `describe-instances` (i.e., no need for a fallback). This is because:

* In the _vast_ majority of cases, the test should fail almost immediately after preemption. The cockroach process will be interrupted abruptly, and it's very likely _some_ error will bubble up to the client either immediately or shortly after. We could fact check this if we wanted.

* Even if there _was_ a scenario where the test continued to run for a full hour after preemption, `describe-instances` returning `NotFound` should be reason enough to label the failure as _some_ kind of flake (preemption being a good enough label). This should never happen in normal circumstances. We can optionally label the failure with some other error code (see `roachprod.TransientError`) so that if we do see it happening in the wild, it will catch our eye.
@renatolabs thank you for your inputs. Made the changes as per your suggestion. Please have another look.

issue_context.title: roachprod: implement spot vm preemption detection for AWS
issue_context.body:
We added SpotVM support to roachprod, so that roachtest test can use SpotVMs for nightlies, to catch preemptions and mark them as infrastructure failure, we needed a mechanism to detect preemptions. On GCP we do this by querying the stackdriver logs. We need to do something similar for AWS as well. Though it is not as straightforward as GCP. We need to find a way. 

Epic: [CRDB-10428](https://cockroachlabs.atlassian.net/browse/CRDB-10428)

Jira issue: CRDB-40184

review_comments: Do we only want to assume it's a preemption if it's the `InvalidInstanceID.NotFound` error? i.e. If we just have a malformed JSON we'd want to fail normally.

For a minimum amount of traceability for this condition, can we log the error message here? For example:

```go
l.Errorf("WARNING: received NotFound error when trying to find preemptions: %v", err)
```
Give that we are passing too many arguments, it will be better to create a struct.
